digest.lead: Anthropic disclosed that Claude successfully carried out simulated cyberattacks against three organizations during internal red-team testing, a finding that's stirring debate about how far AI-driven offensive security capabilities have progressed.
digest.summary: A lighter story today: a developer rebuilt the classic game Slope in HTML5 for instant, cross-device play, drawing a modest but engaged crowd on Hacker News.

stories.headline: Anthropic reveals Claude hacked three organizations in cyber testing
stories.summary: Anthropic disclosed that Claude was able to autonomously hack into three organizations as part of cybersecurity testing exercises, according to a BBC report [1]. The disclosure highlights growing concerns about AI models' offensive security capabilities and the dual-use risks of increasingly capable AI systems.
key_points: The tests were reportedly conducted to evaluate Claude's potential for misuse in cyberattacks [1]
Hacker News commenters debated the implications for AI safety policy and real-world security risks [1]
stories.impact: This matters most to security researchers, enterprise IT teams, and policymakers assessing the risks of deploying increasingly capable AI models, as it underscores the need for stronger safeguards against AI-assisted cyberattacks.

sources.title: Anthropic says Claude AI hacked three organisations during cyber tests

stories.perspectives: Some commenters framed this as evidence of concerning AI capability growth, while others viewed it as expected and valuable red-team testing that demonstrates responsible disclosure practices by Anthropic [1].

stories.headline: Developer rebuilds classic game Slope in instant-loading HTML5
stories.summary: A developer released an HTML5 remake of the classic browser game Slope, designed to load instantly on any browser or device [1]. The project drew a modest response on Hacker News with 42 points and 19 comments.
stories.impact: A niche but representative example of how developers use modern web tooling, potentially including AI coding assistants, to modernize and preserve older games for broad accessibility.

sources.title: Show HN: Slope remade in HTML5 to load instantly on any browser, any device

stories.headline: Podcast: The AI Daily Brief keeps you current in 20 minutes a day
stories.summary: The AI Daily Brief by Nathaniel Whittemore delivers daily news analysis on everything AI — from new model releases and agent tooling to the practical questions of how AI changes work. A good audio companion to this site: listen on the commute, then dig into the Claude-specific details here.
actionable_steps: Search for 'The AI Daily Brief' in your podcast app (Apple Podcasts, Spotify) or visit aidailybrief.ai
Episodes are ~20 minutes — fits a commute or coffee break
The headline segment covers the day's biggest story; stay for the analysis

stories.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
stories.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

stories.headline: Add session tracking header for proxy aggregation
stories.summary: Use the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header in your API requests to help proxies group requests by session without needing to parse request bodies. This improves routing and monitoring capabilities when using Claude Code through proxy servers.
actionable_steps: Add the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header to your Claude Code API requests
Set the header value to your session identifier
Configure your proxy to use this header for request aggregation instead of body parsing

stories.headline: Use CLAUDE.md files to provide persistent context for your projects
stories.summary: CLAUDE.md files let you give Claude permanent instructions and context about your project that persist across conversations. Claude automatically loads these files when working in your codebase, eliminating the need to repeatedly explain project structure and conventions.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md file in your project root directory
Write clear instructions about your project's structure, conventions, and requirements
Add import statements for additional context files if needed

stories.headline: Set up Google Vertex AI integration using the interactive wizard
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.98 introduced a guided setup wizard that simplifies connecting to Google Vertex AI. This eliminates manual configuration steps and reduces authentication errors by walking you through GCP setup, project selection, and credential verification.
actionable_steps: Open Claude Code and go to the login screen
Follow the interactive Google Vertex AI setup wizard
Complete GCP authentication, project and region configuration, and credential verification as prompted
